questions.q: What is the main difference between val and var?
opts: A val can't be reassigned later, a var can
val is only for numbers, var is for all types
There's no difference, they're the same
var works at compile time, val at runtime
questions.exp: val (value) is a read-only reference — once assigned, it can't be reassigned. var (variable) can be changed. Note: val fixes only the reference, not the object itself — you can still add elements to a mutableListOf held in a val.

questions.q: Which functions does a data class generate automatically?
opts: equals(), hashCode(), toString(), copy() and componentN()
questions.exp: Based on the properties in the primary constructor, a data class automatically generates equals()/hashCode(), toString(), copy() and component1(), component2()… for destructuring.

questions.q: In Kotlin, how must a parent class be declared so that another class can inherit from it?
opts: Nothing is needed, all classes are open to inheritance
Only with abstract — there's no other way
questions.exp: In Kotlin, classes are final (closed) by default. To allow inheritance you have to write open. abstract classes are also open to inheritance, but you can't create objects from them directly.

questions.q: What is the result of this code?
questions.code:
val list = listOf(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
println(list.filter { it % 2 == 0 }.map { it * it })
questions.exp: First, filter picks the even numbers → [2, 4]. Then map squares each of them → [4, 16].

opts: Forces a nullable value to non-null and throws an NPE if it's null
Converts the value to a String
questions.exp: !! is the «not-null assertion» operator. If the value is null, a KotlinNullPointerException is thrown. Since it switches off Kotlin's null safety completely, you should avoid it whenever possible.

questions.q: What does the suspend keyword mean?
opts: The function never returns a value
The function can be paused and resumed later — it's called only inside a coroutine
The function creates a new thread automatically
questions.exp: A suspend function can pause (suspend) without blocking the thread. It can be called only from another suspend function or from a coroutine builder (launch, async, runBlocking). It doesn't create a thread by itself.

questions.q: What is the main difference between apply and also?
opts: apply uses this, also uses it — but both return the object itself
apply returns the object, also returns the lambda result
questions.exp: Both return the receiver object itself. The difference is the context: inside apply you use this (so you can set properties directly), inside also you use it (more readable for side effects).

opts: Yes, Int is converted to Long automatically
No — Kotlin has no automatic number conversion, you need x.toLong()
Yes, but it will give a warning
Only when working together with Java
questions.exp: Unlike Java, Kotlin doesn't support automatic widening number conversion. You have to write x.toLong() explicitly — this prevents hidden data loss.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of a sealed class?
opts: All subclasses are known at compile time — no else needed in a when expression
questions.exp: Since all subclasses of a sealed class are defined in the same module, the compiler knows every one of them. This makes the when expression exhaustive — no else branch is needed, and the compiler warns you when you add a new subclass.

questions.q: Which types can't be used with lateinit?
questions.exp: lateinit doesn't work with primitive types (Int, Long, Double, Boolean, Char…), because they have no null value to mark the «not assigned yet» state. Use by Delegates.notNull() for them instead.

questions.q: Which statement about extension functions is true?
opts: They give access to the class's private members
They're resolved statically — not virtual, can't be overridden
They can be added only to classes you wrote yourself
questions.exp: Extension functions add nothing to the class — the compiler turns them into ordinary static function calls. That's why they're not polymorphic (they're chosen by the declared type of the variable) and have no access to private members.

questions.q: What is the result of this code?
questions.code:
val a = listOf(1, 2, 3)
val b = listOf(1, 2, 3)
println(a == b)
println(a === b)
questions.exp: == checks structural equality (equals) — the two lists have the same elements, so it's true. === is referential equality — these are separate objects, so it's false.

questions.q: What does the Unit type in Kotlin correspond to?
opts: Java's void — but Unit is a real type
questions.exp: Unit is the counterpart of Java's void, but in Kotlin it's a real type with exactly one instance. If a function returns nothing, it returns Unit by default — you don't need to write it.

questions.q: What is async/await used for in coroutines?
opts: Doing work in parallel and getting the result later — it returns a Deferred
questions.exp: async returns a Deferred<T> and starts the work right away. When you call await(), it waits for the result without blocking the thread. Starting several async calls at once gives you real parallelism.
